request.spec:
Each person's row shows, for every period, a carried figure: the due of their claims that count
which belong to a period ending before this period starts and were still OPEN or
PENDING at the end of this period (by the status log, as the period figures count). A period with
nothing carried shows 0.00.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now shows a carried figure for every period, but `bin/e2e` doesn't fully pass yet: 3 of the 4 tests pass, and the 4th fails because of a mistake in the spec, not the app.

**What changed** (front end only; no stored data or server changes were needed):
- **`src/main/frontend/features/periods/periods.ts`** has a new function, `personPeriodCarried`. It adds up the dues of the person's claims that count by the same rules the period figures use (`countedAt`), keeping only claims that:
  - have a due-by date inside an earlier period, one that ends before this period starts, and
  - were still OPEN or PENDING at the end of this period, going by the status log.

  Dues are worked out the same way as the period due-totals, so a period with nothing carried shows `0.00`.
- **`src/main/frontend/features/periods/periods.slot.tsx`** shows the figure next to each period's due-total on the person's row, as `data-testid="person-period-<name>-carried"`.

**The failing test:** "carried figures scenario 3" stops at `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts:1131`. That line expects the parent-sheet field to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`, which is a placeholder that was never filled in. The app correctly shows `<sheet id>-p`. I'm not allowed to edit the spec, so it will keep failing until someone corrects that line.

To check the rest of that scenario, I ran a temporary copy of the spec with only that one line corrected. All 4 tests passed in the copy, including every assertion after line 1131. I deleted the copy afterwards, so `e2e/specs/` only has the original spec.

**To run the tests yourself:** something else on this machine is already using port 3002, which is what your `PORT` is set to. On that port the tests hit the other app and fail at the very first steps. I ran them with `PORT=3217 bin/e2e`.
